title: Craft cell floor ignores ungauged entities: 2 of 12 gauged reads as the step
body:
## Summary
craftForCell takes the worst projected gauge over the entities that HAVE a craft verdict; entities with an artifact and no gauge are ignored, so a partly gauged step shows a level it never measured for most of its entities.

## Description
src/lib/craft/craftCell.ts:292 filters `mine` to verdict rows only and src/lib/craft/craftCell.ts:303 takes the worst of those; `contentByEntity` (built per step in src/lib/status/statusReads.ts:111-124 from every artifact row) is consulted only for staleness. The docstring at src/lib/craft/craftCell.ts:272 says "the map states the floor, never the best case", but an ungauged entity is the A0 floor (quality-verdict-integrity: no positive claim without a measurement). Fixed: an entity present in contentByEntity with no verdict projects A0 (because "entity not gauged"), or the cell carries a gauged/total coverage count the chip renders.

## Flow
- craft loop gauges 2 exemplar bestiary entities for "AI Behavior" at A2
- statusReads builds contentByEntity for all 12 entities
- craftForCell returns A2 for the cell; 10 ungauged entities are invisible
- fix: fold ungauged entities in as A0 (or expose coverage) and pin with a test

## Expected impact
Operators reading the /status A-axis stop seeing a level for steps that were sampled, not gauged. Could break: if the craft loop intends exemplar gauging, every partly gauged cell drops to A0 and the campaign needs a coverage-aware display instead.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the A-axis chip never claims a level for unmeasured entities
Before: 14 of 351 gauged cells in ~/.pof/pof.db are partial (e.g. bestiary::AI Behavior gauged 2/12 shows A2, bestiary::3D & Rig 2/12 shows A1)
After: predicted 0 of 351 cells show a level above A0 without full coverage (or the 14 cells carry a 2/12 coverage mark)
Method: probe - read-only SQL over craft_verdicts vs pipeline_artifacts entity counts; fix not built because it changes a display contract read by statusReads (outside this context)
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Operators reading the /status A-axis stop seeing a level for steps that were sampled, not gauged. Could break: if the craft loop intends exemplar gauging, every partly gauged cell drops to A0 and the campaign needs a coverage-aware display instead.
instrument: craftForCell test: 1 A4 verdict + contentByEntity of 3 entities must not project A4; re-run the statusReads probe counting partial cells

title: Craft A-level trend compares across lens versions, mirror of verdictTrend
body:
## Summary
buildCraftTrend labels a cell improved/regressed from last-minus-first rung across the whole kept log without checking that both points share a lens version or auditor model.

## Description
src/lib/craft/craftCell.ts:139 computes delta = rank(last) - rank(first) and src/lib/craft/craftCell.ts:149 maps it to a direction, although every point carries lensVersion and model (src/lib/craft/craftCell.ts:112-116). The R-axis twin src/lib/judge/verdictTrend.ts:87 has this exact defect recorded as an eval-harness deviation in .ai/registry-map.json; the craft mirror is unrecorded. A lens bump (lens-versions.ts) would read as product movement. Fixed: compute the trend over the comparable window (points sharing the newest lensVersion), or report direction none with a reason when first and last differ in version.

## Flow
- bump a lens to v2 in lens-versions.ts and re-gauge a cell
- GET /api/craft-verdicts attaches movement A1 -> A3 "improved"
- the movement is a rubric change, not a craft change
- fix both trend builders with one comparable-window rule

## Expected impact
A craft campaign cannot be credited with movement a lens bump produced. Could break: craftMovementLabel copy for cells whose history spans a bump (none today).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a trend direction is only stated between comparable gauges
Before: 0 multi-point craft histories exist today (all lenses v1, no cell has >1 history row) - latent
After: predicted: a v1->v2 history reports no direction instead of improved
Method: simulation - three walked cases (same version: unchanged; v1->v2 rise: falsely improved today; model swap at same version); no live multi-point history exists to probe
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A craft campaign cannot be credited with movement a lens bump produced. Could break: craftMovementLabel copy for cells whose history spans a bump (none today).
instrument: buildCraftTrend test with points at lensVersion 1 then 2 (and two models) asserting direction is not improved/regressed; apply the same rule to buildVerdictTrend

title: Calibration drift reports the provisional-inclusive rate, not the enforced one
body:
## Summary
calibrationDrift computes rateDelta from run.overall (provisional seeds included) and never from run.confirmed, the only rate evaluateCalibration enforces; it also compares runs across RUBRIC_VERSION without saying so.

## Description
src/lib/judge/calibration.ts:330 rateDelta = next.overall.rate - prev.overall.rate; the enforced figure is run.confirmed.rate (src/lib/judge/calibration.ts:275). With 3 provisional seeds (src/lib/judge/calibration.ts:95-99) mixed in, a drop in human-confirmed agreement can be masked in the drift line judge-run prints (scripts/judge-run.ts:530-532). Fixed: add confirmedRateDelta (null when either side has no confirmed scored) and a rubricChanged flag; print both.

## Flow
- run --calibrate twice; confirmed labels drift while provisional seeds hold
- judge-run prints "+0pp" from overall
- operator reads no drift on the enforced number
- fix: additive confirmedRateDelta + rubricChanged, printer updated

## Expected impact
The operator sees drift in the number that gates the build. Could break: nothing reads rateDelta except the judge-run print line.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - drift is reported on the enforced figure
Before: 0 drift fields derived from run.confirmed; 1 consumer (scripts/judge-run.ts:532)
After: 1 confirmed-rate delta + rubric flag reported
Method: simulation - walked (a) equal overall, confirmed -20pp -> today +0pp; (b) rubric v3->v4 runs -> a silent cross-rubric delta; (c) no confirmed -> null either way. No persisted calibration history on this machine to probe
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The operator sees drift in the number that gates the build. Could break: nothing reads rateDelta except the judge-run print line.
instrument: calibrationDrift test: two runs with equal overall rate but confirmed rate down 20pp must surface a confirmed delta; scripts/judge-run.ts:532 prints it

title: judge-run.ts keeps its own judgeClassOf copy beside the exported rejudgePlan one
body:
## Summary
The deliverable-class -> judge-class rule that keys stored verdicts exists at src/lib/judge/rejudgePlan.ts:33, scripts/judge-run.ts:291 and inline at scripts/judge-run.ts:403; the preview and the run must agree on it.

## Description
rejudgePlan.judgeClassOf keys the ?plan=1 preview (src/app/api/judge-verdicts/route.ts:39 via planPriorKey), while judge-run uses a private copy to key priors and an inline ternary to write `judge`. The rejudgePlan docstring claims the preview "can never disagree with the run"; that holds only while three copies agree by hand. Fixed: judge-run imports judgeClassOf from @/lib/judge/rejudgePlan at both sites.

## Flow
- add a deliverable class judged by llm-panel in one copy only
- preview keys priors one way, the run another
- preview says "never judged" for steps the run skips
- fix: one exported definition, two imports

## Expected impact
Removes a silent preview/run disagreement source. Could break: nothing; identical logic.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of the judge-class rule
Before: 3 definitions (rejudgePlan.ts:33, judge-run.ts:291, judge-run.ts:403 inline)
After: 1 definition, 2 call sites
Method: probe - grep of the predicate across src/ and scripts/; not built because scripts/judge-run.ts is outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Removes a silent preview/run disagreement source. Could break: nothing; identical logic.
instrument: grep: count definitions of the text-config -> llm-panel predicate (today 3); after the import, 1

title: Admission lets a current-rubric judge PASS through with no dimension scores
body:
## Summary
admitJudgeVerdict refuses a sub-band pass but admits a non-human current-rubric pass that carries no per-dimension scores, although the rubric output contract requires them and the "weakest dimension caps" rule cannot be audited without them.

## Description
src/lib/judge/admission.ts:42 checks score >= BANDS.shippable only; dimensions are optional at src/app/api/judge-verdicts/route.ts:90 and scripts/judge-run.ts omits them when the parsed map is empty. A pass with nothing itemised is a holistic number with no evidence of what was measured (judge-contract-design: dimensions, not a vibe; quality-verdict-integrity). Honest floor holds: only passes are refused. Fixed: a non-human pass at RUBRIC_VERSION must carry at least one dimension (ideally every DIMENSIONS[cls] key).

## Flow
- judge returns {score:93, verdict:pass, dimensions:{}}
- judge-run posts without dimensions
- route admits; statusModel can verify-green the step
- fix: admission refuses the dimensionless pass; the step stays unjudged and is re-drawn

## Expected impact
No step turns verified-green on an un-itemised score. Could break: fixtures and any writer posting dimensionless current-rubric passes (none found in scripts/).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every elevating pass is itemised
Before: 0 of 21 stored v4 passes lack dimensions (323/323 v4 rows carry full key coverage) - the door is open but unused
After: door closed: a dimensionless v4 non-human pass is a 400
Method: probe - read-only SQL over judge_verdicts (rubric_version, verdict, dimensions); not built in-round because it is M (door + two test fixture files)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/lib/judge/admission.ts:42  if (v.verdict === 'pass' && rubric === RUBRIC_VERSION && v.judge !== 'human' && v.score < BANDS.shippable)
src/app/api/judge-verdicts/route.ts:90  dimensions: z.record(...).optional(),
probe: rv4 pass llm-panel n=21 nodims=0
impact: No step turns verified-green on an un-itemised score. Could break: fixtures and any writer posting dimensionless current-rubric passes (none found in scripts/).
instrument: admission test: v4 llm-panel pass at 95 with dimensions absent/{} is refused; update the dimensionless pass fixtures in src/__tests__/lib/judge/admission.test.ts and src/__tests__/api/verdict-admission-routes.test.ts

title: JudgeResult.verdict keeps the model's word even when it contradicts the score
body:
## Summary
parseJudgeResult returns the model's verdict field verbatim; judge-run re-derives pass/fail from the median score, but judge-one (the green-loop in-loop probe) prints the raw verdict, so the two harnesses can disagree on the same draw.

## Description
src/lib/judge/rubrics.ts parseJudgeResult copies o.verdict; scripts/judge-run.ts:400 overrides it with score >= BANDS.shippable; scripts/judge-one.ts:137 prints res as-is. The rubric states verdict = pass only if overall >= BANDS.shippable, so the score is the authority. Fixed: derive verdict in the parser from the clamped score (keep the model's word as modelVerdict for diagnostics).

## Flow
- judge draw returns score 86, verdict pass
- judge-one prints PASS 86
- judge-run posts FAIL 86
- fix: parser derives the verdict once

## Expected impact
In-loop probes stop reporting passes the official run will not record. Could break: benchmark scripts read score only (model-benchmark.ts:356, capability-benchmark.ts:112), so low.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one verdict rule from score
Before: 2 verdict sources (model field via parse/judge-one, score rule in judge-run.ts:400)
After: 1 (score rule in the parser)
Method: probe - read of the 5 parseJudgeResult consumers; not built because it changes the JudgeResult contract seen by scripts outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
scripts/judge-run.ts:400  const verdict = res.score >= BANDS.shippable ? 'pass' : 'fail';
scripts/judge-one.ts:137  console.log(JSON.stringify({ ...res, rubricVersion: RUBRIC_VERSION }));
impact: In-loop probes stop reporting passes the official run will not record. Could break: benchmark scripts read score only (model-benchmark.ts:356, capability-benchmark.ts:112), so low.
instrument: parseJudgeResult test: {score:50, verdict:'pass'} yields verdict 'fail' (derived from BANDS.shippable); judge-one output re-checked

title: No dimension floor gates a judge pass (gating-floors)
body:
## Summary
The rubric tells the judge that "a single broken dimension caps the asset", but nothing enforces it: a 92 overall with one dimension at 40 is admitted and can verify-green.

## Description
src/lib/judge/rubrics.ts dimensionBlock asks the judge to let weak dimensions dominate; admission (src/lib/judge/admission.ts:42) and judge-run (scripts/judge-run.ts:400) gate on the overall score alone. The registry technique gating-floors (llm-observability/judge-contract-design) makes pass a conjunction: overall >= threshold AND no dimension under its floor. Choosing the floor value (BANDS.placeholder? per-dimension?) is a rubric policy call and would bump RUBRIC_VERSION.

## Flow
- decide a floor (e.g. every dimension >= BANDS.placeholder for a pass)
- encode it in admission and in judge-run verdict derivation
- bump RUBRIC_VERSION and re-run calibration

## Expected impact
A shippable verdict can no longer hide a broken dimension. Could break: steps whose pass relies on one weak dimension go back to fail (0 today).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - pass is a conjunction with dimension floors
Before: 0 of 21 stored v4 passes have any dimension < 70 (read-only SQL)
After: unmeasurable until the floor value is chosen
Method: probe - SQL over judge_verdicts; the benefit depends on a floor value only the rubric owner can set
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/lib/judge/rubrics.ts dimensionBlock: "a single broken dimension caps the asset"
src/lib/judge/admission.ts:42 (overall score only)
probe: passWithLowDim = 0 of 21
impact: A shippable verdict can no longer hide a broken dimension. Could break: steps whose pass relies on one weak dimension go back to fail (0 today).

title: Nothing couples a NON_CONTENT_KEYS change to a CONTENT_HASH_SCHEME bump
body:
## Summary
contentHash.ts requires a scheme bump on ANY change to the excluded keys, but payload.test.ts pins the key set alone and verdictContentBinding.test.ts pins the scheme alone; adding a key and updating its pin leaves old hashes compared across rules.

## Description
src/lib/judge/contentHash.ts:51 (VOLATILE_KEYS = NON_CONTENT_KEYS) and :67 (CONTENT_HASH_SCHEME = v3, "Bump it with ANY change to VOLATILE_KEYS"). src/__tests__/lib/judge/payload.test.ts:35 pins the four keys; nothing fails if the scheme stays at v3 after a key is added, and every stored v3 hash would then be compared under a different rule (verdicts silently restale - the documented _provenance failure).

## Flow
- add a key to NON_CONTENT_KEYS
- update payload.test pin
- forget the scheme bump; every v3 verdict compares across rules
- fix: one pin over (scheme, keys)

## Expected impact
A key edit cannot land without an explicit scheme decision. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the scheme-bump rule is enforced
Before: 0 tests force the scheme to move with NON_CONTENT_KEYS
After: 1 test forces the pair to move together
Method: simulation - walked the v2->v3 history (src/lib/judge/contentHash.ts:60-66), where the scheme bump was done by hand
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A key edit cannot land without an explicit scheme decision. Could break: nothing.
instrument: pin test of { scheme: CONTENT_HASH_SCHEME, keys: [...NON_CONTENT_KEYS].sort() } together, so a key edit fails unless the scheme moves in the same change
